realism_constraints: No advanced forensic DNA analysis or modern electronic surveillance
Limited rapid communication; telegraph and letters are primary
Transportation mainly by horse, early motor vehicles, and ships
location: England, primarily London and surrounding areas including Berkshires, Park Lane, and the West Highlands
crime_subtype: forged will and staged murder to cover inheritance fraud

cast.name: Sir Henry Marquis
cast.public_persona: Chief of Criminal Investigation Department of Scotland Yard
cast.private_secret: keen intuitive investigator with deep knowledge of criminal methods

cast.name: Mr. Anthony Gosford
cast.public_persona: Englishman claiming bequest in Marshall's will

cast.name: Mrs. Butler
cast.public_persona: wife of the butler accused of murder

surface_summary: A butler is accused of murdering his employer after a robbery of a large sum of money. Circumstantial evidence and expert testimony point to the butler's guilt, but a young woman and a detective uncover inconsistencies suggesting a more complex plot involving a forged will and a left-handed murderer.
accepted_facts: The victim, Mr. Marsh, was found stabbed in the left shoulder.
The butler was present at the time and had no alibi.
A large sum of money was taken from the victim's desk.
Mr. Percy Thompson, the victim's nephew, is left-handed.
inferred_conclusions: The butler committed the murder during a robbery.
The footprints and blood evidence are genuine and indicate the crime scene.
Mr. Percy Thompson is innocent and only interested in the inheritance.
mechanism_description: Mr. Percy Thompson, the left-handed nephew, murdered Mr. Marsh by stabbing him in the left shoulder while the victim sat at his desk. The butler was framed by circumstantial evidence, including a forged will and planted money. The left-handedness of the wound and the dropped glove reveal the true culprit.
delivery_path: Thompson enters the victim's library quietly from the butler's pantry.
He approaches the victim from behind, holding the knife in his left hand.
He delivers a single fatal stab to the left shoulder.
He steals the money from the desk drawer using an ice-pick.
He plants evidence to implicate the butler, including prying open the drawer.
The butler is arrested based on circumstantial evidence.
The young woman and detective expose the inconsistencies and prove Thompson's guilt.
outcome_result: Mr. Percy Thompson is exposed as the murderer and the butler is exonerated.

false_assumption.statement: The butler was guilty of the murder because he was found at the scene with no alibi.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The butler was the only servant present and had opportunity; circumstantial evidence and the forged will pointed to his guilt. The victim's nephew had no apparent motive or suspicious behavior.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It hides the fact that the nephew was left-handed and the wound matches this, and that the butler was framed with planted evidence.

supporting_points: Presence at the crime scene with no alibi
Drawer pried open with an ice-pick from the butler's pantry
Strong circumstantial evidence and expert testimony
Prosecutor's confident case against the butler
false_solution.the_one_flaw: The wound's position and handedness do not match the butler, and planted evidence was fabricated.

red_herrings.description: The will was altered from 30,000 to 50,000 dollars favoring Gosford, suggesting a motive for forgery.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The will was forged by Gosford to claim more inheritance, unrelated to the murder itself.

red_herrings.description: Bloody footprints found at Benton Court were claimed to be of a barefoot assassin.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The footprints were fabricated using a hand to mislead investigators.

closed_circle.rationale: The suspects are limited to those with access to the victim and knowledge of the will and inheritance; no outsiders had opportunity or motive.

time_anchors: morning of the third of February
time_windows: presence of nephew at crime scene

inference_path.observation: The stab wound is on the left side of the victim's neck and shoulder.
inference_path.correction: Only a left-handed person could have delivered such a wound from the victim's position.
inference_path.effect: This excludes the butler, who is right-handed, as the murderer.
required_evidence: Medical report detailing the position and angle of the stab wound
Witness testimony about the victim's seating and room layout

inference_path.observation: The butler was found at the scene with no alibi and the drawer was forced open with an ice-pick from his pantry.
inference_path.correction: The forced drawer and presence are circumstantial and could be staged.
inference_path.effect: The butler's guilt is questionable; evidence may have been planted.
required_evidence: Analysis of the drawer forcing marks

inference_path.observation: A glove was dropped and picked up by Mr. Percy Thompson, who is left-handed.
inference_path.correction: The glove drop indicates the presence and involvement of Thompson.
inference_path.effect: Thompson's presence at the scene is confirmed and suspicious.
required_evidence: Witness statement about the glove drop

inference_path.observation: The will was altered from 30,000 to 50,000 dollars favoring Gosford.
inference_path.correction: Chemical reagent test revealed the alteration was recent and forged.
inference_path.effect: Gosford forged the will to claim a larger inheritance.
required_evidence: Chemical reagent test results on the will document

inference_path.observation: The butler's attorney withdrew from the case citing loss of confidence.
inference_path.correction: The withdrawal was due to pressure and manipulation by Gosford.
inference_path.effect: The defense was compromised, affecting the trial's fairness.

inference_path.observation: The young woman presents a detailed drawing of the crime scene and points out inconsistencies.
inference_path.correction: Her observations reveal the true sequence of events and the murderer's identity.
inference_path.effect: The court reconsiders the evidence and suspects Thompson.
required_evidence: Drawing on the menu card showing room layout
Courtroom testimony of the young woman

inference_path.observation: Thompson is left-handed and the wound matches left-handed attack.
inference_path.correction: This physical evidence directly implicates Thompson as the murderer.
inference_path.effect: Thompson is identified as the true culprit.

discriminating_test.design: Recreate the crime scene with the victim seated at the desk and the suspect approaching from the butler's pantry. Test which hand can deliver a fatal stab to the left shoulder as found. Examine the glove drop and the position of the drawer forcing marks to verify if the butler could have committed the crime or if it was staged.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals that only a left-handed person could have made the wound, excluding the butler. It also shows the forced drawer marks are consistent with the impact of the victim's body and not forced entry, indicating staging.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The stab wound can only be replicated by a left-handed attacker from the butler's pantry side, and the drawer forcing marks cannot be duplicated by the butler's tools or actions.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the crime scene, the wound, the room layout, and the suspects' handedness. The drawing on the menu card and the testimony about the glove drop are presented before the solution. The chemical analysis of the will and the inconsistencies in the footprints and blood stains are also disclosed. These clues allow an attentive reader to deduce the true culprit.
